questions.stem: A 26 year old primigravida at 10 weeks gestation attends her first antenatal visit. She has no medical comorbidities and takes no regular medication. Which supplement is recommended routinely for all pregnant women in the first trimester to reduce the risk of fetal neural tube defects?
questions.explanation: Periconceptional folic acid supplementation reduces the incidence of neural tube defects and is recommended for all women planning pregnancy and through the first trimester. Iron is routinely offered later in pregnancy for anaemia prophylaxis rather than to prevent structural malformations, and high dose vitamin A is teratogenic.

questions.stem: A 30 year old woman at 34 weeks gestation has a blood pressure of 152/98 mmHg on two occasions four hours apart. Urine dipstick shows 1+ protein. She has no headache, visual disturbance or right upper quadrant pain. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: New onset hypertension after 20 weeks with significant proteinuria defines pre-eclampsia, even in the absence of severe features. Gestational hypertension is hypertension without proteinuria or other organ dysfunction, so the proteinuria makes that label incorrect here.

questions.stem: A 24 year old woman in the second stage of labour has been pushing for 45 minutes. The fetal head is visible at the introitus and does not recede between contractions. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
options: Apply fundal pressure to accelerate delivery
Administer a tocolytic to delay delivery
Prepare for delivery and encourage controlled pushing with the next contraction
questions.explanation: Crowning with a head that does not recede between contractions indicates imminent vaginal delivery, so the woman should be supported to deliver with controlled pushing. Caesarean section at this station would be hazardous and unnecessary, and fundal pressure risks uterine rupture and shoulder dystocia.

questions.stem: A 28 year old woman delivers a term infant after a prolonged second stage. Ten minutes after delivery of the placenta she has heavy vaginal bleeding with a soft, poorly contracted uterus. What is the most common cause of this presentation?
questions.explanation: Uterine atony is the commonest cause of primary postpartum haemorrhage, and the soft poorly contracted uterus with heavy bleeding is characteristic. Genital tract trauma typically causes bleeding despite a well contracted uterus, and retained tissue usually presents with a retained placenta or later secondary haemorrhage.

questions.stem: A 42 year old woman has a 6 cm solid, mobile mass in the right breast with no skin changes and no palpable axillary nodes. Which investigation provides the definitive tissue diagnosis?
options: Core needle biopsy of the mass
questions.explanation: Core needle biopsy gives histology, grade and receptor status, which are required for planning breast cancer treatment. Fine needle aspiration cytology can suggest malignancy but cannot reliably distinguish invasive from in situ disease or provide receptor information, so it is not definitive here.

questions.stem: A 24 year old woman who suffers from migraine with aura asks for advice about contraception. She does not smoke and has no other medical problems. Which method is contraindicated for her?
questions.explanation: Migraine with aura is a recognised contraindication to combined hormonal contraception because of the additive risk of ischaemic stroke. Progestogen-only methods such as the implant, injection and copper device do not carry this oestrogen related thrombotic risk and remain suitable options.

questions.stem: A 32 year old woman at 36 weeks gestation presents with a blood pressure of 168/112 mmHg, a severe persistent headache and 3+ proteinuria. She has had no convulsions. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
options: Give a single dose of oral nifedipine and reassess in 24 hours
Perform an immediate caesarean section before any medication
Admit, give intravenous magnesium sulphate and antihypertensive therapy, and plan delivery
Discharge with oral labetalol and review in one week
questions.explanation: This is pre-eclampsia with severe features, so magnesium sulphate for seizure prophylaxis, blood pressure control and timely delivery are all indicated. Simple outpatient oral therapy with delayed review is unsafe because eclampsia and stroke risk are high, and delivery should follow stabilisation with magnesium and antihypertensives rather than precede it.

questions.stem: A 29 year old woman at 39 weeks gestation has spontaneous rupture of membranes with clear liquor. After 8 hours she is having irregular contractions and the cervix is 4 cm dilated. The fetal heart trace is normal. What is the most appropriate management?
options: Await spontaneous labour for a further 24 hours
questions.explanation: Prolonged rupture of membranes with inadequate contractions and a normal fetal trace is managed by augmenting labour, which shortens the interval to delivery and reduces infection risk. Expectant waiting for a further 24 hours increases chorioamnionitis risk, and caesarean section is not indicated when the trace is normal and the cervix is already dilating.

questions.stem: A 31 year old woman at 34 weeks gestation has a painless episode of bright red vaginal bleeding. Her uterus is soft and non-tender, the fetal heart is normal and ultrasound shows the placenta covering the internal os. Which action is contraindicated?
questions.explanation: In suspected placenta praevia a digital vaginal examination can provoke catastrophic haemorrhage and is absolutely contraindicated until the placental site is known. Monitoring, intravenous access and steroids are all appropriate because the priority is maternal stabilisation and preparation for delivery.

questions.stem: A 26 year old woman is admitted at 8 weeks gestation with lower abdominal pain and light vaginal bleeding. She is haemodynamically stable. Ultrasound shows an empty uterine cavity and a left adnexal mass with free fluid in the pouch of Douglas. Beta hCG is 1,800 IU/L. What is the most appropriate management?
options: Expectant management with repeat hCG in one week
Reassurance and discharge without follow up
questions.explanation: An empty uterus with an adnexal mass and free fluid in a woman with a positive hCG indicates a tubal ectopic pregnancy, and surgical management is appropriate given the free fluid suggesting rupture or significant haemoperitoneum. Expectant management is only suitable for small, unruptured cases with low and falling hCG, and mifepristone alone is not effective treatment for ectopic pregnancy.

questions.stem: A 35 year old woman with a body mass index of 34 has had regular unprotected intercourse for 14 months without conceiving. Her cycles are irregular at 45 to 60 days. Which initial investigation is most likely to identify the cause?
options: Serum follicle stimulating hormone, luteinising hormone and testosterone
questions.explanation: Irregular long cycles with obesity suggest anovulation, most commonly polycystic ovary syndrome, so a hormone profile including gonadotrophins and testosterone is the key initial test. Hysterosalpingography assesses tubal patency and is part of the workup but does not explain the ovulatory disturbance, and laparoscopy is invasive and reserved for specific indications.

questions.stem: A 58 year old postmenopausal woman presents with a two month history of postmenopausal bleeding. She is obese and has type 2 diabetes. Transvaginal ultrasound shows an endometrial thickness of 12 mm. What is the most appropriate next step?
options: Reassurance as bleeding is common after menopause
questions.explanation: Postmenopausal bleeding with a thickened endometrium requires endometrial sampling to exclude endometrial carcinoma, for which obesity and diabetes are strong risk factors. Expectant repeat scanning or hormone therapy would delay diagnosis, and postmenopausal bleeding is never considered normal.

questions.stem: A 33 year old woman at 39 weeks gestation in active labour becomes suddenly hypotensive and hypoxic, and the fetal heart rate drops to 60 beats per minute. She has a tense uterus and dark vaginal bleeding. Coagulation studies later show a prolonged clotting time. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Placental abruption with disseminated intravascular coagulation
questions.explanation: Painful bleeding with a tense uterus, fetal compromise and coagulopathy is the classic picture of severe placental abruption complicated by disseminated intravascular coagulation. Uterine rupture usually follows a previous scar and presents with loss of station and tearing pain, while vasa praevia causes fetal bleeding with a usually non-tender uterus.

questions.stem: A 30 year old woman at 38 weeks gestation has a seizure lasting 90 seconds in the labour ward. Her blood pressure is 176/118 mmHg and she is confused afterwards. Which drug should be given first to control and prevent further seizures?
questions.explanation: Magnesium sulphate is the drug of choice for eclampsia because it is more effective than diazepam or phenytoin at preventing recurrence and has a better maternal and perinatal safety profile. Labetalol lowers blood pressure but has no anticonvulsant action, and diazepam is only a second line alternative when magnesium is unavailable.

questions.stem: A 34 year old woman at 41 weeks gestation in the second stage of labour has a prolonged deceleration of the fetal heart rate to 70 beats per minute lasting four minutes. The cervix is fully dilated at station plus one with a cephalic presentation. What is the most appropriate immediate action?
options: Start an oxytocin infusion to speed delivery
Perform a fetal scalp blood sample before deciding
Arrange immediate operative delivery by caesarean section
Continue pushing and reassess in 30 minutes
questions.explanation: A prolonged deceleration with a profoundly low baseline indicates acute fetal hypoxia, so the fetus must be delivered without delay; with the head high at station plus one, caesarean section is the fastest safe route. Continuing to push or augmenting with oxytocin prolongs hypoxia, and scalp sampling is not done during an acute unresolving bradycardia.

questions.stem: A 38 year old woman with a body mass index of 41 has had three consecutive first trimester miscarriages. She has irregular menses and ultrasound shows a polycystic ovarian appearance. Which factor is most strongly associated with recurrent miscarriage in this woman?
options: Insulin resistance and obesity related hyperinsulinaemia
A history of using combined oral contraceptives
questions.explanation: Obesity and insulin resistance are recognised contributors to recurrent pregnancy loss, and weight reduction and metformin are often used to improve the metabolic environment before conception. A retroverted uterus is a normal variant and does not cause miscarriage, and previous contraceptive use has no established causal link.

questions.stem: A 62 year old woman has a fixed, hard mass in the left breast with peau d orange and palpable matted axillary nodes. Core biopsy confirms invasive ductal carcinoma. Staging shows multiple small lung metastases. What is the most appropriate initial treatment approach?
options: Systemic therapy directed by receptor status with endocrine therapy if hormone receptor positive
Modified radical mastectomy followed by observation
questions.explanation: Metastatic breast cancer is treated systemically, with choice guided by oestrogen receptor, progesterone receptor and HER2 status, and surgery is reserved for palliation or local control. Mastectomy alone would not address disseminated disease and would delay effective systemic treatment.

questions.stem: A 44 year old woman has a 9 cm firm pelvic mass arising from the pelvis, ascites and a raised CA125. At laparotomy there is a solid ovarian mass with peritoneal seeding. Frozen section suggests a germ cell tumour in a woman of this age. Which tumour marker should be measured to support the diagnosis and monitor treatment?
questions.explanation: Non-seminomatous germ cell tumours of the ovary secrete beta hCG and alpha fetoprotein, and these markers are used both diagnostically and to monitor response to chemotherapy. CA125 is non-specific and raised in many ovarian and non-ovarian conditions, while inhibin B is the marker for granulosa cell tumours.
